subject: design/existing-repo-onboarding-v2
statement: `adopt` is a **layer over converge, not a rewrite of it** (`design-brainstorm:existing-repo-onboarding-tech-design#D-1` · `#ALT-1`). It consumes converge's ownership-class classification as the single source of tree-vs-manifest truth — one classifier, so no second list drifts (AP-11; the failure `docs/observability/incidents.md#I5` records) — and owns the adoption-specific concerns on top: the plan, the collision resolutions, the epoch, and undo. converge's steady-state `Run` is not overloaded with one-time adoption semantics (NR-2). The **adoption plan** is one durable, closed-schema receipt (`adoption-plan/v1`) in the engine's system namespace, rendered human-readable for review, with a lifecycle draft (`adopt`) → applied (`apply` stamps it with the undo-data) → consumed (`undo`) — the agreement and the receipt are one artifact (`#D-2`). The **install-epoch** is the already-present `epoch.commit`, consumed by the tree-local gates through a single `git diff --name-only epoch..HEAD` filter at scan-set construction, so grandfathering costs O(changed-set), never O(corpus) (`#D-3`). Collisions resolve **additive-adjacent where an honest mechanism exists** — hook chaining, a distinct workflow filename — and **by named instruction where none does** (an existing root convention file); nothing the repo owns is rewritten (`#D-4`; NG-3). **Undo removes the installation and preserves post-adoption work**, failing closed on operator-edited artifacts (`brainstorm:existing-repo-onboarding#D-11`). A reader who stops here knows the shape: **one classifier, one durable plan-receipt, an epoch-scoped gate, and a reversible install that never touches what the repo owns.**
